Alex: Heads-up: after the kernel-selector tweak that prefers the new fused-attn kernel, we started seeing comm/compute overlap vanish on 8xA100 TP/PP jobs. Allreduce queues pile up and CUDA graph replay sometimes hangs. Repro is pretty stable on staging.
Maya: Which commit? do you have a small repro?
Alex: commit 3f9a2d6, the change is in kernel_selection.cc where we pick 'fused_attn_v2' for seq_len<=512. Repro command: `./deploy_staging --model llama-13b --tp 2 --pp 4 --batch 8 --profile`.
Chris: Any nvprof / nvtx trace? curious if compute is actually waiting or if NCCL is blocking because streams aren't overlapping.
Alex: nvtx timeline attached (paste):
```
Time (ms):
GPU0: [compute: 0-145] [idle:145-210] [compute:210-400]
GPU1: [compute: 0-120] [nccl_allreduce:120-190] [compute:190-400]
Host: nvtx markers show graph capture start at 5ms, capture end at 18ms, replay at 200ms
```
Pattern: GPU compute sections are non-contiguous and large gaps coincide with NCCL waits on some ranks. The capture/replay windows look misaligned with prefetch kernels.
perf-bot: PERF ALERT: nightly-staging p99 latency +18% vs baseline on multi-gpu long-seq jobs (tag: kernel-selector).
Maya: Did anything change in KV cache prefetching? That code does its own stream management. If prefetch uses an external stream not captured into the cudaGraph, replay can reorder and cause host syncs.
Alex: Yes — I tweaked kvcache prefetch to use a dedicated non-blocking stream to avoid blocking main compute. The intention was better overlap, but maybe it breaks capture semantics.
Jen: If capture was started on the main stream and prefetch uses an external `cudaStreamNonBlocking` that isn't captured, captured graph will not include the prefetch ops -> during replay, prefetch either runs out-of-order or forces host syncs. Try binding prefetch to the capture stream or use `cudaStreamAttachMemAsync` semantics.
Chris: Another angle: the new fused kernel has different kernel launch order and longer op durations; that can shift when we schedule allreduce and reduce overlap opportunities. Combined with an uncaptured prefetch, it could make NCCL schedule later, increasing stall.
Leo: Quick mitigation: set env `REDWOOD_DISABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` on the failing fleet to force the eager path. That avoids capture/replay mismatches at cost of some perf.
Alex: Trying that now on staging. Also running `nvprof --trace` with `--gpu-trace` to get kernel launch vs nccl timeline.
Maya: If you can reproduce, try this patch locally:
```
--- a/runtime/kvcache/prefetch.cc
+++ b/runtime/kvcache/prefetch.cc
@@
-  cudaStream_t s = create_nonblocking_stream();
-  launch_prefetch(s, ...);
+  // Use the current capture-aware stream so prefetch becomes part of cudaGraph
+  cudaStream_t s = get_current_capture_stream_or_fallback();
+  launch_prefetch(s, ...);
```
It forces prefetch to be part of capture when capture is active. If capture isn't active, fallback is non-blocking.
Alex: Good idea. Will try. Also bisecting kernel selector change to see which specific heuristic flipped the timeline.
Chris: Also check if `cudaGraphLaunch` is synchronizing internally in our older driver; there's a known driver quirk where launching many small graphs can serialize NCCL scheduling. Which driver version on staging?
Alex: Driver 530.41, CUDA 11.8. We saw similar but not identical behavior on 535 in dev.
Jen: If the workaround is to bind prefetch to capture stream, add a unit test ensuring prefetch NVTX markers fall inside the same capture window. That should prevent regressions when kernel selection changes launch patterns.
perf-bot: NOTE: adding a canary job that toggles `REDWOOD_DISABLE_CUDAGRAPH` and kernel-selection variant could help quantify the perf/latency tradeoff automatically.
Leo: I'll roll a quick canary with disabled graphs for the flagged customers and keep telemetry.
Alex: Preliminary: disabling graphs restores overlap and p99 drops back to baseline. With the prefetch-binding patch locally, replay looks sane in nvtx. Opening PR with patch + test and will link the perf run.
Maya: Awesome. If bisect shows kernel selection ordering is the amplifier, we should add heuristics to avoid kernel combos that produce large prefetch -> long compute gaps unless prefetch is guaranteed captured.
Alex: Agreed. I'll include a short-term guard: if kvcache prefetch not capture-aware, prefer the old attn kernel.
Chris: Nice. Keep us posted. Thanks for the fast turnaround. :thumbsup:
Alex: Will follow up with PR and attach nvprof traces. Thanks everyone.
